criterion_notes.c1: Examines household sanitation systems, wastewater disposal (sewerage, septic tanks, open street discharge), and basic water and electricity access in the informal settlement Bajo Los Anonos.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Plain reading: YES — the study explicitly adopts a social, technical, and institutional perspective, interviewing a municipal environmental manager about local government plans, surveying residents on housing tenure and perceived municipal assistance, and referencing municipal regulatory plans, past evictions, and CNE/Ministry of Health inhabitability declarations. Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: NO — the empirical analysis does not examine a rule-type legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access (such as tenure or documentation eligibility requirements for utility connection, tariffs/cost-recovery rules, administrative burdens, or utility regulatory structure). Instead, it characterizes household wastewater self-management and O&M practices, compares street wastewater BOD5 to environmental discharge limits (Decreto Ejecutivo N°33601), links wastewater disposal to self-reported illness, and notes a generic lack of municipal plans or project support.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical data from a stratified survey of 51 residents (aged 15+), laboratory BOD5 testing of 3 community wastewater grab samples, and an open-ended interview with the environmental manager of the Municipality of Escazú.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports household-level service access and sanitation outcomes, including water and electricity coverage (100%) and disposal pathways for brownwater (43% septic tank, 33% open street discharge, 14% sewerage, 10% unknown) and greywater (47% open street discharge, 27% sewerage, 16% septic tank, 10% unknown).
criterion_notes.c5: Identifies the population and sample (51 surveyed residents across three sectors of Bajo Los Anonos, San José, Costa Rica; unit of analysis: respondent/household and 3 wastewater sampling points), study design (cross-sectional mixed-methods case study), and sanitation access/management outcomes, though institutional exposure is limited to general absence of municipal project intervention rather than a rule-type mechanism.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with an English abstract); per Inclusion Criterion 10, direct assessment and translation from the Spanish full text are feasible.

evidence_quotes.quote: Mediante la aplicación de encuestas a los habitantes del lugar, se realizó una caracterización técnica y social de la autogestión del saneamiento en la comunidad; además, se realizó un muestreo simple de aguas residuales en tres puntos distintos de la comunidad; finalmente, se realizó una encuesta con preguntas abiertas al gestor ambiental de la Municipalidad de Escazú para conocer su perspectiva.

Respecto al manejo de las aguas pardas, el 43% lo realizaba mediante tanque séptico; un 33% la disponía a cielo abierto, ya sea en la calle, acequia, lotes o el río; un 14% iba al alcantarillado y un 10% dijo desconocerlo.

Al consultarles si alguna institución les ha ofrecido ayuda para tratar de solucionar el tema de aguas residuales, un 86% dijo que no, mientras que otro 14% mencionó que en algunas ocasiones la municipalidad había realizado ciertos trabajos.

El acceso a información por parte de la municipalidad fue difícil y no se logró obtener una respuesta definida sobre el futuro del asentamiento informal. La comunidad se encuentra a la espera de una resolución de la Comisión Nacional de Emergencias (CNE), la cual se refiere a este lugar con respecto al riesgo, principalmente por deslizamientos.

Acorde con el objetivo planteado, así como los resultados alcanzados y la discusión general al respecto, concluimos que la comunidad presenta problemas en cuanto a la correcta gestión de las aguas residuales. Esto se debe a una combinación de factores como la falta de acceso a sistemas de saneamiento de calidad, malas prácticas de los vecinos y las vecinas y falta de apoyo por parte de la municipalidad para garantizar que la población viva en un ambiente limpio.

raw_response.exposure: Community wastewater self-management practices, O&M knowledge, and general absence of municipal sanitation support/plans (no specific legal or administrative rule governing service access analyzed)
raw_response.outcome: Household wastewater disposal/sanitation access (sewer connection, septic tank use, open street discharge), basic water/electricity access, self-reported illness frequency, and street wastewater BOD5 levels
raw_response.population_and_sample: Inhabitants aged 15+ in the informal settlement Bajo Los Anonos, Escazú, San José, Costa Rica (n = 51 stratified resident surveys; 3 wastewater grab samples; 1 municipal environmental manager interview)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification to Criterion 2. Although the paper empirically characterizes household sanitation access/wastewater disposal in an informal settlement in Costa Rica and includes a brief municipal perspective on the lack of local government intervention (which would satisfy a broad literal reading of 'institutional factor' under Criterion 2), it does not analyze any specific legal, regulatory, or administrative rule-type mechanism governing service access (such as land-tenure or documentation eligibility rules for sewer connection, tariffs, administrative burdens, or enforcement of connection rules). Instead, its empirical analysis focuses on household self-management and septic tank O&M practices, wastewater BOD5 levels relative to effluent discharge standards, resident health perceptions, and the general absence of municipal plans/projects.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional mixed-methods descriptive case study (resident survey, wastewater BOD5 grab sampling, and key-informant municipal interview)
